tagline: Istanbul's cultural and entertainment backbone — İstiklal Caddesi, rooftop bars, live music venues, galleries, and the city's best nightlife.

items.name: Kıraathane İstanbul
items.description: A beautifully restored historic reading room turned café and cultural space. Stunning interior, excellent coffee, rotating art exhibitions.

items.name: Kahve Dünyası (İstiklal)
items.description: A Turkish coffee chain done right. The İstiklal branch is conveniently placed for a mid-walk stop.

items.name: Gramofon Café
items.description: A cosy café near Tünel with live music on weekends and an eclectic crowd of artists and regulars.

items.name: Asri Turşucu
items.description: A legendary pickle and meze shop that's been here for over a century. The turşu suyu (pickle juice) is an acquired taste that locals swear by.

items.name: Boncuk Restaurant
items.description: A long-standing Armenian-influenced meyhane in Çiçek Pasajı area. Excellent mezes, warm atmosphere, very local crowd.
items.tip: Nevizade Sokak (off İstiklal) is worth visiting for the street atmosphere alone — lined with meyhanes.

items.name: Zübeyir Ocakbaşı
items.description: One of the city's best charcoal grill restaurants. The Adana kebap and lamb ribs are outstanding. Book ahead.
items.tip: Dinner only. The open charcoal grill is a great experience — ask to sit near it.

items.name: 360 İstanbul
items.description: Rooftop bar and restaurant with a 360° panoramic view of Istanbul. Spectacular at night. Book well ahead.
items.tip: The view from the rooftop at night is genuinely one of the best in the city. Worth the reservation effort.

items.name: Nevizade Sokak
items.description: A pedestrian alley off İstiklal packed with meyhanes, live music bars, and tables spilling onto the street. The heart of Beyoğlu nightlife.

items.name: Salon İKSV
items.description: Istanbul's premier live music and performance venue. Excellent programming — international and Turkish artists.

items.name: İstiklal Caddesi
items.description: Istanbul's most famous pedestrian boulevard. 1.4km of shops, cafés, galleries, churches, and street life. The nostalgic red tram runs its length.
items.tip: Weekday mornings are far more pleasant than weekend afternoons. The side streets off İstiklal are where the real Beyoğlu lives.

items.name: Pera Museum
items.description: An outstanding private museum with excellent Turkish and international art. The Orientalist painting collection is world-class.

items.name: Çiçek Pasajı
items.description: A 19th-century covered flower market turned bar-restaurant arcade. Atmospheric, lively, and touristy in the best way.

tips: İstiklal Caddesi is pedestrian-only. The Tünel funicular connects the bottom (Karaköy) to the top in 90 seconds.
The side streets off İstiklal — Nevizade, Bekar, Balo — are where the best restaurants and bars hide.
Avoid the main drag on Saturday evenings unless you like large crowds. The parallel streets are always less busy.
The F2 nostalgic tram on İstiklal is slow but charming — great for photos, not great if you're in a hurry.
